description: A guitar chord source: twenty-eight chords laid out in four rows of seven, each played as six string pitches with a mute gate per string, plus a capo, a whammy bar and a per-string pitch bend

params.text: Picks which of the seven chords in the current row is played, 1 to 7
Picks which of the four rows of chords is used, 1 to 4
Switches the first of the two alternative fingering banks on each press, which changes every chord's voicing
Switches the second of the two alternative fingering banks on each press, which changes every chord's voicing
Transposes every string in semitones, -12 to 12, the way a capo does
Plays that chord on each press, setting both the row and the chord within it

inputs.text: Picks the chord within the current row, one step per volt, added to the chord knob; the menu can read it as a volt per octave instead
Picks the row, one step per volt, added to the row knob
Transposes every string in semitones, one semitone per volt, added to the capo knob and taken as a whole number
A voltage above 0.05V flips the first fingering bank from whatever its button has it at, rather than replacing it
A voltage above 0.05V flips the second fingering bank from whatever its button has it at, rather than replacing it
Bends that string sharp, a tenth of a semitone per volt, taken as an absolute value so a negative voltage bends sharp as well
Bends every string sharp at once, a fifth of a semitone per volt, taken as an absolute value so a negative voltage bends sharp as well

outputs.text: That string's pitch as a volt per octave, with the capo, the whammy bar and that string's bend added; a muted string carries the chord's root a semitone below instead
Carries 10V while that string is muted in the current fingering and 0V while it sounds, which the menu can turn the other way round
The root of the current chord as a volt per octave, with the capo added
A 1ms 10V trigger whenever the chord changes

notes: a cable in the first string output alone makes it a six-channel polyphonic cable; patching any of the other five turns them all back to one channel, and the mute outputs behave the same
the two chord bank buttons work together, so the four combinations of them give four fingerings of each chord; the panel display names the fingering each combination gives
the strings a chord does not use are not silent: they carry the chord's root a semitone below, so the mute output is what says which strings to play
menu: Classical Chord Set — swaps the whole grid of twenty-eight chords for a second set
CHORD input in V/oct — reads the chord input as a volt per octave, picking the chord from a note rather than one step per volt
Invert Mute Gate Outputs — makes each mute output carry 10V while its string sounds and 0V while it is muted
